newsitem.title: UK: Late bond market prices - December 5.
newsitem.headline: Late bond market prices - December 5.

text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bunds sank in late dealings to their lowest levels this week, after U.S. Treasuries dipped following U.S jobless claims data. Dealers said the upward trend was still intact, however. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.59, down 0.88 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - British gilts settle sharply lower, shaken by sterling's depreciation after Bank of England Governor Eddie George's remarks that rate rises were not needed urgently. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-22/32, down 29/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bonds slipped as a lack of follow-through buying at a government bond auction and mild disappointment that German rates were left unchanged punctured earlier optimism sparked by weak German data. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.20, down 0.34 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian cash debt market ended fractionally on the firmer side of unchanged after earlier gains were pared. Futures started to suffer in late trade, although dealers said Italian markets had held up slightly better than others. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.42, down 0.22 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were down sharply on technically motivated selling. The 30-yr T-bond yield was the highest since November 8 close, with nothing to fuel further gains until data on Friday and next week. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 114/14/32, down 29/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.47 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended the Tokyo session higher, after plunging early in the morning on remarks by a former senior Finance Ministry official, traders said. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.20, up 0.82 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - A jumbo mark deal from Spain headed a list of sovereign bonds launched during an active session. Spain, said to have also been eyeing dollars and yen, launched a 2.0 billion mark 10-year offering at a reoffer spread of 24 basis points over the April 2006 Bund through Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
